recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source change is needed for FHIR-16450 unless a later work-group decision changes the broader delete/referential-integrity policy.
issue_request: FHIR-16450 was a Published FHIR-I STU3 change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked that the HTTP delete section clarify that servers may or may not enforce business rules when deleting resources that are referenced by other resources.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 14174, imported as git commit a1cd05b722493b8dbd36926a33a9e17ef2b98192, which added the requested referenced-resource deletion sentence to source/http.html. Later commit 7b129e2288476995a7a73ac45b0c50a18f3c257a changed only the restricted wording from "MAY NOT" to "might not" while preserving the server-discretion meaning.
additional_context: The current source/http.html delete interaction still says deletion support is policy/business-rule dependent, that resource-specific refusal such as referential integrity should return 409 Conflict, and that servers MAY choose to enforce business rules for deletion of referenced resources but might not do so. Later FHIR-24888 is related background about discovering references with _revinclude=* and does not reverse the delete-section discretion. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-16450 found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit on the combined branch because the current active source already satisfies the Jira resolution.

related_jiras.note: Later Published FHIR-core issue about discovering resources that reference a target; it supports the same referential-integrity context but does not change the HTTP delete rule.
